column42: groundwater_nearest_well_km= the straight line distance between the pincode's coordinate and closest well
column44: groundwater_current_depth_m_bgl= how many meters below the goundlevel the water currently sits
column45: groundwater_score_0_10=Severity score->groundwater_trend_m_per_year via band_for_trend() — ≥0.5 m/yr → 10, ≥0.2 → 7, roughly stable (−0.2 to 0.2) → 4, recovering (<−0.2) → 2.
column47: groundwater_confidence-> normal-nearesr well within 50km or else low- nearest well is far aay
column48: nearest_tide_gauge- name of the nearest gauge stations and is blank if there is blank for inland pincodes
column49: nearest_gauge_km- Distance from the pincode to the nearest gauge station
column51: sealevel_score_0_10=anchored against the global IPCC AR6 average (~3.7mm/yr) rather than an Indian government threshold — ≥5.0 → 10 (Extreme), ≥3.5 → 7 (High), ≥1.5 → 4 (Moderate), below that → 2 (Low).
column53: sealevel_confidence-"normal", "low (nearest tide gauge is far away)" beyond 150km, or "not_applicable" for inland pincodes
column54: coast_erosion_pct_of_district_coastline-what percentage of that pincode's district's total coastline NCCR classified as actively eroding, comparing 1990 to 2016 satellite measurements
column55: coastal_erosion_score_0_10-0–10 severity score: ≥50% → 10, ≥35% → 8, ≥20% → 6, ≥10% → 4, below 10% → 2. Blank for any pincode whose district wasn't matched
column56: coastal_erosion_band-"Severe," "High," "Moderate-High," "Moderate," "Low," or "Not Applicable (not one of NCCR's 66 coastal districts)"
column61: river_erosion_band
column62: forestfire_num_qualifying_events=he count of FSI-qualifying fire events (≥3 proximate pixels, same day, inside forest cover, after industrial-source exclusion) found within this pincode's buffer radius, across the full study window.
column63: forestfire_years_with_event=how many distinct calendar years had at least one qualifying event within this pincode's buffer, out of the total years the study spans. Same logic as flood's "% of years" frequency — one event or ten events in the same year still only counts that year once.
column64: forestfire_frequency_pct=years_with_event ÷ total_years_in_window × 100. This is the frequency half of the frequency+intensity split — what percentage of the whole study period saw at least one qualifying fire nearby.
column65: forestfire_max_frp_mw=the single highest Fire Radiative Power (in megawatts) of any qualifying event within this pincode's buffer, across all years.
column66: forestfire_frequency_percentile=his pincode's frequency_pct, ranked as a percentile only against other pincodes that also had at least one qualifying event (not the full national dataset) — the fix from script 20c that prevents any-event-at-all from automatically counting as "high frequency."
column67: forestfire_intensity_percentile=same idea, applied to max_frp_mw — how this pincode's worst fire compares to other fire-affected pincodes' worst fires, not to all of India.
column68: forestfire_verdict=the combined 4-tier label from frequency×intensity percentiles (Frequent-and-severe / Frequent-but-mild / Rare-but-severe / Rare-and-mild), same structure as flood/heat/drought's combine() logic — or "No qualifying events in study window" for the majority of pincodes with zero events at all (a real "not affected," distinct from "not assessed," since every pincode nationally was checked against the full event dataset).
column69: forestfire_buffer_km=the buffer radius actually used to produce this row (20km, per script 20c/20f's final calibrated value) — carried in the output itself so anyone reading the file later knows exactly which buffer setting produced these numbers, without needing to check the script separately.
